label: <DEL> when the first token to copy is p/r/1/j/k/m/z/f/o/a, plus copy-phase input 1
explanation: Never fires in the original-input phase. Its activation is split between the <DEL> step (43% of mass, active on 25% of delimiters) and the copy phase (57%). At <DEL> the rate depends on which token is about to be output (orig(0)): it is high for p, r, 1, j and k (rates 0.22-0.33) and lower for m, z, f, o and a, and higher for short sequences (L=3,4). In the copy phase the clearest trigger is the digit 1 fed back as input (precision about 0.79). The strongest activations of all are 1 as the input on the step right after <DEL> (e.g. sequences starting with 1). The remaining copy-phase activations are weaker and spread out, mostly on the first 1-3 copy steps when the first token is one of the same preferred tokens. These are not captured. It does not fire on original-phase tokens, and it rarely fires on <DEL> when the first token is outside the preferred set. Dev F1 is 0.58 and mass recall 0.69.
